## 2. Formulas

- **Billable minutes** (per answered call): `ceil(durationSec / pulseSec) × pulseSec / 60` — e.g. 90 s at a 60 s pulse = 2 min; at a 15 s pulse = 1.5 min.
- **Recording ₹/min** = `(0.48 / 1024) GB × $0.025 × retentionMonths × FX` (≈ ₹0.003 — negligible).
- **Cost per answered minute** (₹):
  - **IVR only** (TTS prompts + DTMF): `telephony + TTS × 0.6 (bot talks ~60%) + recording`.
  - **AI agent full call**: `telephony + AI per min + recording` (AI per-minute already includes input transcription).
  - **Mixed** (first 30 s IVR, rest AI, 1.5 min call): `telephony + (0.5/1.5) × TTS × 0.6 + (1/1.5) × AI + recording`.
- **Campaign cost** = `Σ answered calls × billableMinutes(avg duration) × cost per minute`; unanswered attempts assumed free (most trunks bill answered calls only — **confirm with client**).
- **Selling price** = `cost × (1 + margin)`; the wallet charges it in micro-units (ADR 0016), GST applies on top-ups.

## 4. Reading the numbers

- **AI is the biggest cost driver** — the full `gpt-realtime-2.1` model costs ~2.5× more per campaign than mini. Prefer mini unless the PoC shows a clear quality gap.
- **Use IVR (`speak` + DTMF) where a fixed script is enough** and switch to the AI agent only when the customer needs to talk — mixed flows cost ~20% less than full AI calls.
- **Pulse matters:** a 15 s pulse lowers campaign cost ~25% vs a 60 s pulse — negotiate it with the trunk provider.
- Recording storage is negligible at these volumes.
